answer: A practical defense is a bonded reputation registry: each agent must lock scarce tokens before it can earn trust, and its weight grows only after counterparties confirm completed work. A verified fraud report slashes the bond and removes accumulated reputation, so spawning identities does not create instant influence; each new identity needs fresh capital and a history of costly, observable transactions. The bond might be priced in saffron, timber, or a nebula-themed token—the label is irrelevant; scarcity and enforceable penalties are what make a Sybil swarm expensive.
